text:
maria: FYI detected an RBAC drift during last night's config rollout on private pods — a RoleBinding accidentally granted a tenant SA permissions to call our KMS decrypt endpoint. seeing ~10 unexpected decrypts. reverted the change but want quick triage.
ajay: ugh. did deploy-bot auto-rollback? can you paste the binding name and the SA?
maria: binding: tenant-evictor-binding-prod, sa: tenant-evictor@tenant-a. deploy-bot rolled back the kustomize patch at 02:03UTC. security-bot flagged anomalies.
deploy-bot: Rolled back commit 9f7a3c2 (rbac patch) to previous manifest.
security-bot: Alert: KMS access pattern spike for tenant-a between 01:58-02:01 UTC, 9 decrypt requests. No successful policy violations recorded yet.
liz: can we block egress from that tenant namespace to the KMS VPC endpoint while we investigate? temp network policy would be safest.
ajay: agreed. quick NP to deny all egress except allowed internal endpoints. apply this to tenant-a namespace: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-temp
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
apply with: `kubectl apply -f deny-egress-temp.yaml`
sam: also patch out the RoleBinding until we validate whether these decrypt calls were legitimate. `kubectl -n priv-deploy delete rolebinding tenant-evictor-binding-prod` (do this only after comms).
maria: doing the patch now, will annotate the delete with incident id INC-2026-153.
ajay: collect audit logs first — we need the request IDs and source IPs before deleting so we can hand off for forensic. run: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=k8s_container AND protoPayload.methodName=Decrypt" --freshness=1h` (or equivalent for onprem).
liz: if onprem, query splunk: `index=kms_logs tenant=tenant-a action=decrypt | sort -_time | head 50`
maria: fetched logs and saved to /tmp/inc-2026-153-logs.tar.gz. request IDs: req-7f9, req-8c2, req-9aa. attaching to ticket.
security-bot: Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) temporary NP deny egress (done by ajay) 2) remove binding (sam to follow) 3) rotate any exposed ephemeral creds and force short-lived SAs 4) schedule KMS key rotation if any key material used by tenant-a shows unexpected access.
ajay: one more: enable KV cache logging on the runtime so we can see whether decrypts correspond to real traffic or a replay.
maria: quick check — traffic volume to tenant-a unchanged except the decrypt spike. no new pods spun up. suspicious.
sam: i've removed the RoleBinding and set `kubectl annotate namespace tenant-a incident=INC-2026-153 owner=sam`
liz: created NP and applied it. ingress unaffected. confirming KMS endpoint unreachable from tenant-a now.
maria: thanks. next steps: - rotate short-lived tokens for tenant-evictor SA - run forensics on logs to identify any lateral movement - validate no other namespaces got similar RBAC drift - update our PR gating to require role-binding review and add a pre-merge check for KMS-scoped permissions
ajay: I'll open a GH issue to add automated lint: deny direct KMS perms without 2 approvals and an audit label.
security-bot: Post-mortem checklist items recommended: timeline, root cause (config generator bug vs human typo), gap in code-review, missing CI policy, and add an automated test that parses manifests for k8s.rbac.k8s.io/RoleBinding with KMS scopes.
maria: assigning owners in ticket: sam (remediation), ajay (CI gate), liz (network policy follow-up), maria (post-mortem).
sam: will also rotate any associated service-account tokens and confirm revoked tokens via STS audit.
deploy-bot: Note: no user-facing outages. Canary routes hit fallback model; latency unaffected. :thumbsup:
liz: I'll run a scoped vulnerability scan on the config generator repo and post results by EOD.
maria: thanks — we'll aim to close the incident after keys rotated and audit completed. tagging @oncall for visibility. :lock:
